title: Beyond the qubit count: how to read a quantum computing headline
summary: A bigger processor is only part of the story. Reliability and the work a machine can actually perform matter too.
author: Quantum Research Center

sections.heading: What is being counted?
paragraphs: A physical qubit is a component of a quantum processor. A logical qubit encodes quantum information across physical qubits so that errors can be detected and corrected. The two counts describe different things.

sections.heading: Reliability changes the picture
paragraphs: A useful comparison asks how reliably a processor preserves information and performs operations, and how long it can keep a computation running. Error correction must operate repeatedly during computation; a single successful demonstration does not establish every capability needed for larger applications.

sections.heading: Three questions to bring to the next announcement
paragraphs: Are the reported qubits physical or logical? Which operations were demonstrated, and with what error rates? What resources and running time would the proposed application require?
These questions help separate a hardware milestone from evidence of practical usefulness. A company roadmap describes an intended destination; the experiment shows what has been achieved so far.
